The recursion gives \(f(n)=f(\lfloor n/2\rfloor)+(n\bmod 2)\), so \(f(m)\) is the number of 1s in the binary representation of \(m\).

Since \(2010<2047=2^{11}-1\), the maximum number of binary digits that can be 1 is at most 10. This is achieved by \(m=1023=2^{10}-1\), whose binary representation has ten 1s.

Thus the greatest possible value is \(\boxed{10}\).
